paragraphs.title: Abandoning the Lord and Shishak’s Invasion

answers: Rehoboam and all Israel
Shemaiah and the princes
Shishak and his army
easy.explanation: The verse says that Rehoboam and all Israel forsook the law of the LORD.
easy.q: Who forsook the law of the LORD?

answers: Jeroboam
Shishak king of Egypt
Iddo the seer
easy.explanation: Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

answers: The king’s house
The fenced cities of Judah
The treasures of the Temple
easy.explanation: Shishak took the fenced cities which pertained to Judah and then came to Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Shishak take before coming to Jerusalem?

answers: The invasion came because they had forsaken the LORD
The invasion came because new cities had been built
The invasion came after Rehoboam died
medium.explanation: The passage connects Shishak’s attack with Israel’s transgression against the LORD.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between forsaking the LORD and Shishak’s attack?

answers: Shishak marched to war against Judah
Shishak became king in Egypt
Shishak came to Jerusalem to rule there
medium.explanation: In context, the phrase describes Shishak’s military campaign against Judah.
medium.q: What does “Shishak came up against Jerusalem” mean in this context?

answers: He reached Jerusalem first and then took the cities
He took the fenced cities first and then came to Jerusalem
He conquered Egypt first and then Judah
medium.explanation: The passage says that he took the fenced cities and came to Jerusalem.
medium.q: What was the order of Shishak’s advance?

answers: It was a large and diverse military force
It was a small group of messengers
It consisted only of soldiers from Judah
challenge.explanation: The army included many people, chariots, horsemen, and several foreign peoples.
challenge.q: What does the description of Shishak’s army suggest?

answers: Shishak came as far as Jerusalem
Rehoboam reigned seventeen years
Shemaiah was a prophet
challenge.explanation: Reaching Jerusalem shows that the invasion went far beyond Judah’s borders.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the invasion reached the heart of Judah?

answers: To spread the law of the LORD
To take treasures and spoil
To appoint a new king over Judah
challenge.explanation: The following verses say that Shishak took the treasures of the LORD’s house and the king’s house.
challenge.q: What appears to have been the main purpose of the campaign according to the rest of the chapter?

answers: Shemaiah the prophet
Shishak the king
Iddo the seer
easy.explanation: Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah.
easy.q: Who explained the reason for the invasion to Rehoboam and the princes?

answers: They fled from Jerusalem
They humbled themselves and said that the LORD was righteous
They declared a new war
easy.explanation: They humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is righteous.”
easy.q: How did the king and the princes respond to the prophet’s words?

answers: Not to destroy them altogether
To give them victory over Shishak
To return all their treasures immediately
easy.explanation: The LORD said that He would not destroy them but would grant them some deliverance.
easy.q: What did the LORD decide after seeing that they humbled themselves?

answers: They had forsaken the LORD
They had lost their treasures
They wanted to enlarge Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Shemaiah declared that they had forsaken the LORD, and therefore He had left them in Shishak’s hand.
medium.q: What was the reason for the invasion according to Shemaiah?

answers: They submitted and acknowledged the LORD’s justice
They defeated the Egyptian army
They silently left Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Their humility was shown by their submission and their confession that the LORD was righteous.
medium.q: What does it mean that the princes and king “humbled themselves”?

answers: They would become servants and learn the difference between serving the LORD and serving earthly kingdoms
Jerusalem would be destroyed without anyone escaping
All Israel would be carried away to Egypt
medium.explanation: The LORD said they would be Shishak’s servants so that they would know the difference between His service and the service of other kingdoms.
medium.q: What limited punishment was mentioned by the LORD?

answers: The punishment was limited instead of being complete destruction
Shishak immediately ended his entire campaign
Judah received all the fenced cities back
challenge.explanation: Because they humbled themselves, the LORD would not destroy them altogether, although punishment remained.
challenge.q: What changed because Rehoboam and the princes humbled themselves?

answers: They recognized that the judgment was justified
They claimed that the invasion had nothing to do with them
They rejected the prophet’s message
challenge.explanation: Their statement acknowledges the LORD’s justice in allowing the punishment.
challenge.q: What does the statement “The LORD is righteous” reveal about the leaders’ response?

answers: They still became servants and experienced loss
They immediately began ruling Egypt
They received Shishak’s treasures
challenge.explanation: The LORD spared them from total destruction but still allowed them to become servants and suffer the effects of the invasion.
challenge.q: Why did mercy not remove all the consequences of their actions?

paragraphs.title: The Plunder and Replacement of the Gold Shields

answers: All the treasures
Only the priests’ garments
Only the prophets’ books
easy.explanation: The passage says that Shishak took all the treasures from both houses.
easy.q: What did Shishak take from the house of the LORD and the king’s house?

answers: Gold
Brass
Iron
easy.explanation: Shishak carried away the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
easy.q: What were the shields made of that Solomon had made?

answers: Silver shields
Brass shields
Wooden shields
easy.explanation: Rehoboam made shields of brass instead of the gold shields.
easy.q: What did Rehoboam make instead of the gold shields?

answers: The princes of Judah
The guard
Shishak’s soldiers
medium.explanation: The guard fetched the shields and brought them to the king when he entered the house of the LORD.
medium.q: Who carried the shields when the king entered the house of the LORD?

answers: They served as replacements for the gold shields
They were hidden in Shishak’s house
They were sent to the fenced cities
medium.explanation: Rehoboam made the brass shields in place of the gold shields that had been taken.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the brass shields?

answers: The kingdom was not completely destroyed
Rehoboam immediately lost his throne
Jerusalem was completely abandoned
medium.explanation: The LORD’s wrath turned from Rehoboam so that He would not destroy him altogether.
medium.q: What was the result of Rehoboam’s humility?

answers: The new shields were a simpler replacement for what had been taken
The new shields belonged to Shishak
The new shields were made only to decorate the house of the LORD
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam replaced the valuable gold shields with brass shields after Shishak took them.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the gold shields and the brass shields?

answers: The shields were kept and used ceremonially when the king appeared
They were weapons sent to the front line
They were intended for Shishak’s army
challenge.explanation: The passage describes a regular practice of bringing out the shields for the king and returning them afterward.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the guard bringing out the shields when the king entered the house of the LORD?

answers: Judah suffered punishment, but some good remained among the people
The plunder proved that Judah had committed no sin
The good things caused Shishak to return the gold
challenge.explanation: Although Judah lost its treasures, the passage says that things still went well in Judah, so it was not destroyed altogether.
challenge.q: How do the plunder and the statement that “in Judah things went well” fit together?

answers: In Jerusalem
In Egypt
In Samaria
easy.explanation: Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned there.
easy.q: Where did Rehoboam strengthen himself and reign?

answers: Seven years
Seventeen years
Forty-one years
easy.explanation: Rehoboam reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Rehoboam reign in Jerusalem?

answers: Shishak
Jeroboam
Abijah his son
easy.explanation: After Rehoboam’s death, Abijah his son reigned in his place.

answers: He did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD
He did not build a city in Jerusalem
He did not gather a large army
medium.explanation: The passage says that Rehoboam did evil because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.
medium.q: What was Rehoboam’s spiritual failure despite his strength as king?

answers: The records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer
The books of Shishak and Jeroboam
The records of the royal guard only
medium.explanation: The passage refers to the book of Shemaiah and the writings of Iddo concerning genealogies.
medium.q: In whose records were the acts of Rehoboam mentioned?

answers: His continual wars with Jeroboam
His journeys with Shishak in Egypt
His construction of the gold shields
medium.explanation: The passage says that there were continual wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
medium.q: What was mentioned together with the acts of Rehoboam?

answers: His reign was not spiritually approved
He was considered completely righteous
The passage gives no evaluation of him
challenge.explanation: The passage directly says that Rehoboam did evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the statement “he did evil” reveal about the biblical evaluation of Rehoboam’s reign?

answers: His early abandonment of the LORD agrees with the statement that he did not prepare his heart to seek Him
The end of the chapter says that he completely returned to the LORD
The end of the chapter reveals that he never ruled in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Both sections portray Rehoboam as a ruler who failed to seek the LORD faithfully.
challenge.q: How does the beginning of the chapter connect with the end of Rehoboam’s reign?

answers: It was the city chosen by the LORD to put His name there
It was a city built by Shishak
It was a city located in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is described as the city which the LORD had chosen to put His name there.
challenge.q: What religious and geographical detail is emphasized about Jerusalem?
